open Classical
open Bridges.AlgebraMachineLearning
open Bridges.NeuralProofSpectrum

namespace Bridges.NeuralProofSpectrumDeep

universe u v w

variable {R S K : Type*} {α : Type*}

/-! ## Section 0: the underlying coalgebra and depth-wise agreement

We abbreviate the underlying (unweighted) neural observation system and recall the
definitional identity `neural_behavior (toNeural N) = algBehavior N`.
-/

/-- The underlying coalgebra of an algebraic neural system. -/
def toNeural [Semiring R] [Semiring K] (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) :
    NeuralObservationSystem R α K :=
  weighted_to_neural N.toWeighted

theorem neural_behavior_eq_algBehavior [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (x : R) (w : List α) :
    neural_behavior (toNeural N) x w = algBehavior N x w := rfl

/-- Depth-`k` agreement of two states (agree on all contexts of length `≤ k`). -/
def agreeUpto [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (k : ℕ) (x y : R) : Prop :=
  neural_equiv_upto (toNeural N) k x y

theorem agreeUpto_iff [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (k : ℕ) (x y : R) :
    agreeUpto N k x y ↔ ∀ w : List α, w.length ≤ k → algBehavior N x w = algBehavior N y w :=
  Iff.rfl

theorem agreeUpto_symm [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) {k : ℕ} {x y : R}
    (h : agreeUpto N k x y) : agreeUpto N k y x :=
  fun w hw => (h w hw).symm

theorem agreeUpto_trans [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) {k : ℕ} {x y z : R}
    (hxy : agreeUpto N k x y) (hyz : agreeUpto N k y z) : agreeUpto N k x z :=
  fun w hw => (hxy w hw).trans (hyz w hw)

theorem agreeUpto_mono [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) {j k : ℕ} (hjk : j ≤ k) {x y : R}
    (h : agreeUpto N k x y) : agreeUpto N j x y :=
  fun w hw => h w (hw.trans hjk)

/-- Behavioral equivalence is exactly agreement at every depth. -/
theorem behaviorRel_iff_agree_all [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (x y : R) :
    behaviorRel N x y ↔ ∀ k, agreeUpto N k x y :=
  behaviorRel_iff_all_depth N x y

/-! ## Section 1: separating depth and the graded ultrametric

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
-- Hypothesis H1 (resolving F1).  Define `sepDepth x y = sInf {k | ¬ agreeUpto N k x y}`.
-- When `x ≁ y` the set is nonempty (a separating word of some length exists), so
-- `sepDepth` is a genuine least separating depth and lands *in* the set
-- (`Nat.sInf_mem`).  Guarded by `if behaviorRel` the distance `2^(-sepDepth)` is well
-- defined and strictly positive off the diagonal.
--
-- Insight I1.  The STRONG triangle inequality holds.  Key combinatorial fact:
-- depth-`m` agreement is, for each fixed `m`, an equivalence relation (`agreeUpto_trans`).
-- If `x ≁ z` and `m = sepDepth x z`, then if BOTH `gradedDist x y < gradedDist x z` and
-- `gradedDist y z < gradedDist x z`, we would get `agreeUpto m x y` and `agreeUpto m y z`,
-- hence `agreeUpto m x z` — contradicting `m ∈ {k | ¬ agreeUpto N k x z}`.  Hence the max
-- of the two dominates, which is exactly the ultrametric inequality.
-/

/-- The least observation depth that separates `x` from `y` (`0` by convention when they
    are behaviorally equivalent — guarded away in `gradedDist`). -/
def sepDepth [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (x y : R) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k | ¬ agreeUpto N k x y}

theorem sepDepth_symm [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (x y : R) :
    sepDepth N x y = sepDepth N y x := by
  unfold sepDepth
  congr 1
  ext k
  exact ⟨fun h hh => h (agreeUpto_symm N hh), fun h hh => h (agreeUpto_symm N hh)⟩

/-- If `x ≁ y` the separating set is nonempty, so `sepDepth` realises an actual
    separating depth: `x` and `y` do **not** agree up to `sepDepth N x y`. -/
theorem not_agree_sepDepth [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) {x y : R} (h : ¬ behaviorRel N x y) :
    ¬ agreeUpto N (sepDepth N x y) x y := by
  have hne : {k | ¬ agreeUpto N k x y}.Nonempty := by
    by_contra hc
    apply h
    rw [behaviorRel_iff_agree_all]
    intro k
    by_contra hk
    exact hc ⟨k, hk⟩
  exact Nat.sInf_mem hne

/-- If a depth `j` is below the separating depth, the states agree up to `j`. -/
theorem agree_of_lt_sepDepth [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) {x y : R} {j : ℕ} (hj : j < sepDepth N x y) :
    agreeUpto N j x y := by
  by_contra hc
  have : sepDepth N x y ≤ j := Nat.sInf_le hc
  omega

/-- The **depth-graded observation ultrametric**: distance `0` for behaviorally
    indistinguishable states, else `2^(-d)` where `d` is the least separating depth. -/
def gradedDist [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (x y : R) : ℝ :=
  if behaviorRel N x y then 0 else (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(sepDepth N x y : ℤ))

theorem gradedDist_nonneg [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (x y : R) : 0 ≤ gradedDist N x y := by
  unfold gradedDist
  split_ifs with h
  · exact le_refl 0
  · positivity

theorem gradedDist_self [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (x : R) : gradedDist N x x = 0 := by
  simp [gradedDist, behaviorRel_refl]

theorem gradedDist_comm [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (x y : R) : gradedDist N x y = gradedDist N y x := by
  unfold gradedDist
  rw [sepDepth_symm N x y]
  by_cases h : behaviorRel N x y
  · rw [if_pos h, if_pos (behaviorRel_symm N h)]
  · rw [if_neg h, if_neg (fun hh => h (behaviorRel_symm N hh))]

theorem gradedDist_eq_zero_iff [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (x y : R) :
    gradedDist N x y = 0 ↔ behaviorRel N x y := by
  unfold gradedDist
  split_ifs with h
  · simp [h]
  · constructor
    · intro hz
      exact absurd hz (by positivity)
    · intro hh; exact absurd hh h

/-- Positivity off the diagonal, with the explicit value. -/
theorem gradedDist_of_not_rel [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) {x y : R} (h : ¬ behaviorRel N x y) :
    gradedDist N x y = (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(sepDepth N x y : ℤ)) := by
  simp [gradedDist, h]

/-- The graded ultrametric **refines** the discrete observation pseudometric:
    `gradedDist ≤ obsDist` everywhere (and they share the same kernel). -/
theorem gradedDist_le_obsDist [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (x y : R) :
    gradedDist N x y ≤ obsDist N x y := by
  unfold gradedDist obsDist
  split_ifs with h
  · norm_num
  · have : (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(sepDepth N x y : ℤ)) ≤ 1 := by
      apply zpow_le_one_of_nonpos₀ (by norm_num)
      simp
    simpa using this

/-- The kernel of the graded ultrametric is exactly the proof-spectrum congruence. -/
theorem gradedDist_kernel_eq_congruence [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (x y : R) :
    gradedDist N x y = 0 ↔ (behaviorCongruence N).rel x y := by
  rw [gradedDist_eq_zero_iff]; rfl

/-! ### The ultrametric (strong triangle) inequality

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
-- Result R1 (resolving F1).  The crux is `gradedDist_strong_triangle`.  The helper
-- `agree_of_dist_lt` says: if `gradedDist x y < gradedDist x z` (with `x ≁ z`), then `x`
-- and `y` agree up to `m = sepDepth x z`.  Two regimes: if `x ~ y` it is automatic; else
-- `2^(-sepDepth x y) < 2^(-m)` forces `sepDepth x y > m`, hence `agreeUpto m x y` by
-- `agree_of_lt_sepDepth`.  Combining the two helpers with `agreeUpto_trans` against
-- `not_agree_sepDepth` gives the contradiction, i.e. the strong triangle bound.
-/

/-- If a state `y` is strictly closer to `x` than `z` is, then `x` and `y` agree up to the
    separating depth of `x` and `z`. -/
theorem agree_of_dist_lt [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) {x y z : R} (hxz : ¬ behaviorRel N x z)
    (hlt : gradedDist N x y < gradedDist N x z) :
    agreeUpto N (sepDepth N x z) x y := by
  by_cases hxy : behaviorRel N x y
  · -- behavioral equivalence implies agreement at every depth
    exact (behaviorRel_iff_agree_all N x y).mp hxy _
  · -- strict inequality on the exponentials forces a deeper separation depth
    rw [gradedDist_of_not_rel N hxy, gradedDist_of_not_rel N hxz] at hlt
    have hbase : (1 : ℝ) < 2 := by norm_num
    have hexp : (-(sepDepth N x y : ℤ)) < (-(sepDepth N x z : ℤ)) :=
      (zpow_lt_zpow_iff_right₀ hbase).mp hlt
    have : (sepDepth N x z : ℤ) < (sepDepth N x y : ℤ) := by omega
    have hmlt : sepDepth N x z < sepDepth N x y := by exact_mod_cast this
    exact agree_of_lt_sepDepth N hmlt

/-- **The ultrametric inequality.** `gradedDist` satisfies the strong triangle
    inequality, so the observation distance is a genuine pseudo-ultrametric. -/
theorem gradedDist_strong_triangle [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (x y z : R) :
    gradedDist N x z ≤ max (gradedDist N x y) (gradedDist N y z) := by
  by_cases hxz : behaviorRel N x z
  · rw [(gradedDist_eq_zero_iff N x z).mpr hxz]
    exact le_max_of_le_left (gradedDist_nonneg N x y)
  · -- it suffices that not both legs are strictly shorter than `x`–`z`
    rw [le_max_iff]
    by_contra hcon
    push_neg at hcon
    obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := hcon
    have hxy : agreeUpto N (sepDepth N x z) x y := agree_of_dist_lt N hxz h1
    have hyz : agreeUpto N (sepDepth N x z) y z := by
      have hzx : ¬ behaviorRel N z x := fun h => hxz (behaviorRel_symm N h)
      have hlt : gradedDist N z y < gradedDist N z x := by
        rw [gradedDist_comm N z y, gradedDist_comm N z x]; exact h2
      have hzy := agree_of_dist_lt N hzx hlt
      rw [sepDepth_symm N z x] at hzy
      exact agreeUpto_symm N hzy
    exact not_agree_sepDepth N hxz (agreeUpto_trans N hxy hyz)

/-! ## Section 2: functoriality is non-expansive (Lipschitz geometry)

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
-- Result R2 (geometric functoriality).  In the base file morphisms preserve the kernel.
-- Here we sharpen this to a *metric* statement: an `AlgNeuralHom` is non-expansive for the
-- graded ultrametric.  Reason: depth-`k` agreement is preserved by morphisms (immediate
-- from `algBehavior_map`), so the separating set of the image is contained in that of the
-- source, whence `sepDepth` can only grow, whence the distance can only shrink.
-/

/-- Morphisms preserve depth-wise agreement (they can only merge states). -/
theorem agreeUpto_map [Semiring R] [Semiring S] [Semiring K]
    {N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α} {M : AlgNeuralSystem S K α} (f : AlgNeuralHom N M)
    {k : ℕ} {x y : R} (h : agreeUpto N k x y) :
    agreeUpto M k (f.toFun x) (f.toFun y) := by
  intro w hw
  rw [neural_behavior_eq_algBehavior, neural_behavior_eq_algBehavior,
      ← algBehavior_map f x w, ← algBehavior_map f y w]
  exact h w hw

/-- Morphisms cannot decrease the separating depth. -/
theorem sepDepth_map_ge [Semiring R] [Semiring S] [Semiring K]
    {N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α} {M : AlgNeuralSystem S K α} (f : AlgNeuralHom N M)
    {x y : R} (h : ¬ behaviorRel M (f.toFun x) (f.toFun y)) :
    sepDepth N x y ≤ sepDepth M (f.toFun x) (f.toFun y) := by
  -- the image separates at `sepDepth M`, hence so does the source
  have hsep : ¬ agreeUpto N (sepDepth M (f.toFun x) (f.toFun y)) x y := by
    intro hc
    exact not_agree_sepDepth M h (agreeUpto_map f hc)
  exact Nat.sInf_le hsep

/-- **Non-expansiveness.** An `AlgNeuralHom` is `1`-Lipschitz for the graded ultrametric:
    images are never farther apart than their preimages. -/
theorem gradedDist_map_le [Semiring R] [Semiring S] [Semiring K]
    {N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α} {M : AlgNeuralSystem S K α} (f : AlgNeuralHom N M)
    (x y : R) :
    gradedDist M (f.toFun x) (f.toFun y) ≤ gradedDist N x y := by
  by_cases hM : behaviorRel M (f.toFun x) (f.toFun y)
  · rw [(gradedDist_eq_zero_iff M (f.toFun x) (f.toFun y)).mpr hM]
    exact gradedDist_nonneg N x y
  · have hN : ¬ behaviorRel N x y := by
      intro h
      exact hM (behaviorCongruence_map f h)
    rw [gradedDist_of_not_rel M hM, gradedDist_of_not_rel N hN]
    have hge : sepDepth N x y ≤ sepDepth M (f.toFun x) (f.toFun y) := sepDepth_map_ge f hM
    have hexp : (-(sepDepth M (f.toFun x) (f.toFun y) : ℤ)) ≤ -(sepDepth N x y : ℤ) := by
      simp only [neg_le_neg_iff]; exact_mod_cast hge
    exact zpow_le_zpow_right₀ (by norm_num) hexp

/-! ## Section 3: a primality criterion (resolving F2)

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
-- Hypothesis H2 (resolving F2).  The base file noted that primality of
-- `behaviorCongruence N` fails because the pointwise factorisation
-- `∀ w, b(a,w)=0 ∨ b(b,w)=0` does not pull out the quantifier.  The clean cure is a
-- *faithful observation point*: a single context `w₀` whose vanishing already detects
-- behavioral nullity, `behaviorRel N a 0 ↔ algBehavior N a w₀ = 0`.  Then in an integral
-- domain `K`, `algBehavior N (a*b) w₀ = algBehavior N a w₀ * algBehavior N b w₀ = 0`
-- factors at the single point `w₀`, and faithfulness lifts each branch back to behavioral
-- nullity.  This yields a genuine `PrimeSRCong R` — an honest point of `ProofSpectrum R`.
--
-- Failure analysis F3.  Faithfulness is a real restriction (it forces a "generic
-- point").  Without it, primality can fail even over a field; the conjecture in
-- FUTURE_DIRECTIONS.md asks for the exact class of systems admitting a faithful point.
-/

/-- A **faithful observation point**: a context `w₀` whose vanishing detects behavioral
    nullity (`a` is behaviorally null iff its `w₀`-observation is `0`). -/
def FaithfulPoint [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (w₀ : List α) : Prop :=
  ∀ a : R, behaviorRel N a 0 ↔ algBehavior N a w₀ = 0

/-- **Primality criterion.** With a faithful observation point and an integral-domain
    output, the behavior congruence is prime. -/
theorem behaviorRel_prime_of_faithful [Semiring R] [Semiring K] [IsDomain K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) {w₀ : List α} (hf : FaithfulPoint N w₀)
    {a b : R} (h : behaviorRel N (a * b) 0) :
    behaviorRel N a 0 ∨ behaviorRel N b 0 := by
  have hab : algBehavior N (a * b) w₀ = 0 := (hf (a * b)).mp h
  rw [algBehavior_mul] at hab
  rcases mul_eq_zero.mp hab with ha | hb
  · exact Or.inl ((hf a).mpr ha)
  · exact Or.inr ((hf b).mpr hb)

/-- **The prime functor object.** Under a faithful point and an integral-domain output,
    the behavior congruence upgrades to a `PrimeSRCong R` — a point of the proof
    spectrum. -/
def behaviorPrimeCongruence [Semiring R] [Semiring K] [IsDomain K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) {w₀ : List α} (hf : FaithfulPoint N w₀) :
    PrimeSRCong R where
  toSRCong := behaviorCongruence N
  prime_prop := fun h => behaviorRel_prime_of_faithful N hf h

/-- The prime behavior congruence is, in particular, a point of the `ProofSpectrum`. -/
def behaviorPrimeCongruence_mem_spectrum [Semiring R] [Semiring K] [IsDomain K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) {w₀ : List α} (hf : FaithfulPoint N w₀) :
    ProofSpectrum R :=
  behaviorPrimeCongruence N hf

/-- The vanishing locus of the proof-spectrum point is exactly the behaviorally-null
    states, detected by the faithful point `w₀`. -/
theorem behaviorPrime_vanishes_iff [Semiring R] [Semiring K] [IsDomain K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) {w₀ : List α} (hf : FaithfulPoint N w₀) (a : R) :
    vanishes (behaviorPrimeCongruence_mem_spectrum N hf) a ↔ algBehavior N a w₀ = 0 := by
  exact hf a

/-! ## Section 4: capstone — the deepened comparison

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
-- Summary S1.  Bundling the deepened facts: the graded ultrametric, the discrete
-- pseudometric, the coalgebraic behavioral equivalence, and the proof-spectrum congruence
-- all share one kernel; and the graded distance dominates none of them — it refines the
-- discrete pseudometric while carrying strictly more information (the separating depth).
-/

/-- The deepened comparison: graded ultrametric kernel, discrete pseudometric kernel,
    coalgebraic behavioral equivalence, and proof-spectrum congruence all coincide, and
    the graded ultrametric refines the discrete pseudometric. -/
theorem deep_neural_pseudometric_comparison [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (x y : R) :
    (gradedDist N x y = 0 ↔ obsDist N x y = 0) ∧
    (obsDist N x y = 0 ↔ (behaviorCongruence N).rel x y) ∧
    gradedDist N x y ≤ obsDist N x y := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, gradedDist_le_obsDist N x y⟩
  · rw [gradedDist_eq_zero_iff, obsDist_eq_zero_iff]
  · rw [obsDist_eq_zero_iff]; rfl

# Obstruction Monotonicity under Divisibility

## Main Results

- `primitiveResidueSolution_of_dvd`: If `M ∣ N` and there is a primitive
  residue solution mod N, then there is one mod M.
- `no_primitiveResidueSolution_of_dvd`: Contrapositive — an obstruction at
  M propagates to all multiples of M.

## Key Insight

The natural ring homomorphism `ZMod N →+* ZMod M` (for `M ∣ N`) sends

inheritance from `N` to divisors `M`.

import Mathlib
import Speculative.Beal.Defs

open ZMod

/-! ## Solution Inheritance -/

/-
Solutions descend from `N` to any divisor `M`: if `M ∣ N` and
`a^x + b^y = c^z` has unit solutions in `ZMod N`, then it has
unit solutions in `ZMod M`.
-/
theorem primitiveResidueSolution_of_dvd
    {M N x y z : ℕ}
    (hdvd : M ∣ N)
    (hsol : PrimitiveResidueSolution N x y z) :
    PrimitiveResidueSolution M x y z := by
  rcases hsol with ⟨ a, b, c, ha, hb, hc, h ⟩;
  -- Use the ring homomorphism `ZMod.castHom hdvd (ZMod M) : ZMod N →+* ZMod M`.
  set f : ZMod N →+* ZMod M := ZMod.castHom hdvd (ZMod M);
  exact ⟨ f a, f b, f c, ha.map f, hb.map f, hc.map f, by simpa using congr_arg f h ⟩

/-- **Obstruction Monotonicity**: if no primitive residue solution exists
mod M, then none exists mod any multiple of M. One obstructing modulus
annihilates all its multiples. -/
theorem no_primitiveResidueSolution_of_dvd
    {M N x y z : ℕ}
    (hdvd : M ∣ N)

This cycle established (in `Catalog/Bridges/CategoricalTropicalRipsInterleaving.lean`,
0 sorries, axioms `propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound` only) the order-theoretic
core of persistence stability:

- a Rips filtration `ripsOf` of an **arbitrary symmetric distance** `d : α → α → ℝ`
  (generalizing the instance-bound `ripsGraph` of
  `Applications/PoincareData/MetricFiltration.lean`, related by `ripsMetric_eq_ripsOf`);
- the `δ`-**interleaving** relation `Interleaved`, with `interleaved_refl`,
  `interleaved_symm`, `interleaved_mono`, and the **tropical composition law**
  `interleaved_comp` (shifts add: `δ₁ ⊙ δ₂ = δ₁ + δ₂`);
- the **stability theorem** `rips_stability` (`|d − d'| ≤ δ ⇒ δ`-interleaved) and its
  metric form `rips_stability_dist`;
- the **interleaving (pseudo)distance** `interleavingDist` satisfying the tropical
  valuation / pseudometric axioms `interleavingDist_self`, `interleavingDist_comm`,
  `interleavingDist_triangle`.

The conjectures below are concrete, falsifiable next steps. Each is phrased so that a
follow-up cycle can either produce a Lean theorem or a Lean counterexample.

---

## Conjecture 1 — Sharpness of stability (the converse Lipschitz bound)

**Statement.** For finite `α` with two symmetric distances `d, d'`, the interleaving
distance of their Rips filtrations *equals* a tropical "best matching" of edge-birth
scales:
```
interleavingDist (ripsOf d) (ripsOf d') = sInf { δ ≥ 0 | ∀ x y, |d x y − d' x y| ≤ δ on the relevant edge set }.
```
In particular stability is **tight**: there exist `d, d'` with
`interleavingDist (ripsOf d) (ripsOf d') = ‖d − d'‖_∞`. 

**Test.** Prove `interleavingDist (ripsOf d) (ripsOf d') ≥ f(d,d')` for an explicit
lower bound `f`, complementing the upper bound `rips_stability_dist`; or exhibit a
3-point counterexample where the inequality is strict. *Falsifiable:* a single finite
example with strict gap refutes tightness.

## Conjecture 2 — `interleavingDist` is a genuine extended pseudometric on filtrations

**Statement.** Replacing `ℝ` by `ℝ≥0∞` and dropping the nonemptiness hypotheses,
`interleavingDistExt : (ℝ → SimpleGraph α) → (ℝ → SimpleGraph α) → ℝ≥0∞` is a true
`PseudoEMetricSpace` structure on the type of **monotone** filtrations, with
`interleavingDistExt F G = 0 ↔ F = G` on left-continuous filtrations.

**Test.** Build the `ℝ≥0∞`-valued version, prove `edist`-style triangle/symmetry
unconditionally (the `sInf ∅ = ⊤` convention removes the `Nonempty` hypotheses that are
load-bearing in the current `ℝ` version), and register a `PseudoEMetricSpace` instance.
*Falsifiable:* exhibiting two distinct left-continuous monotone filtrations at distance
`0` refutes the separation half.

**Statement.** A `1`-Lipschitz map `φ : (α, d) → (α', d')` (i.e. `d' (φx)(φy) ≤ d x y`)

on filtrations is **`1`-Lipschitz for `interleavingDist`**. Hence `interleavingDist`
is a functor `(FiniteMetricSpaces, Lipschitz) ⥤ (Filtrations, interleaving)` landing in
the tropical-enriched category of §2.

**Test.** Define the induced filtration map, prove the homomorphism existence, and prove
the contraction `interleavingDist (push φ F) (push φ G) ≤ interleavingDist F G`.
*Falsifiable:* a Lipschitz map increasing some interleaving distance.

**Statement.** The **`π₀`/connected-components** functor applied to `ripsOf d` recovers
the single-linkage (sub-)dendrogram, and the associated "merge-scale" distance
`d_SL x y := inf { ε | x, y connected in ripsOf d ε }` is an **ultrametric**, with
```
interleavingDist (ripsOf d) (ripsOf d') ≤ ‖d_SL − d'_SL‖_∞ ≤ ‖d − d'‖_∞,
```

links this bridge to `Bridges/CategoricalTropicalUltrametric.lean`: `d_SL` is the
ultrametric *reconstructed* from the tropical valuation data of the filtration.

**Test.** Define `d_SL` via `SimpleGraph.Reachable` on `ripsOf d ε`, prove the strong
triangle inequality `d_SL x z ≤ max (d_SL x y) (d_SL y z)`, and prove the chained bound.
*Falsifiable:* a 4-point example violating the ultrametric inequality for `d_SL`.

## Conjecture 5 — Stability of the connectivity (Poincaré) threshold

**Statement.** Define the connectivity threshold `θ(d) := inf { ε | ripsOf d ε is
connected }` (the `MetricFiltration`-level "Poincaré threshold" of the catalog). Then
`θ` is **`1`-Lipschitz** in the `sup`-distance:
```
|θ(d) − θ(d')| ≤ ‖d − d'‖_∞,
```
as a corollary of `rips_stability` plus monotone-connectivity transfer along
interleavings (`δ`-interleaved filtrations have connectivity thresholds within `δ`).

**Test.** Prove "connected at scale `ε` ⇒ connected at scale `ε + δ` for a
`δ`-interleaved filtration" (using `interleaved.fg` and `SimpleGraph.Connected.mono`),
then derive the Lipschitz bound on `θ`. *Falsifiable:* a finite perturbation moving the
connectivity threshold by more than `‖d − d'‖_∞`.

# FUTURE DIRECTIONS — Functorial Tropical Certificates for Berggren–Lorentz Lattice Reduction

This cycle established a **functorial tropical certificate** for the Berggren–Lorentz
monoid acting on Pythagorean triples
(`Catalog/Bridges/TropicalBerggrenCertificate.lean`):

- `rowNorm` — the ℕ-valued L∞ matrix row-norm — is **submultiplicative**
  (`rowNorm_mul_le`).
- Every Berggren generator has row-norm exactly `7` (`rowNorm_gen`).
- `wordMatrix` is a genuine **monoid homomorphism** `(List, ++) → (GL₃ℤ, *)`
  (`wordMatrix_append`), making the certificate functorial.
- Consequently a depth-`d` triple has all coordinates `≤ 5·7^d`
  (`berggren_hypotenuse_certificate`), and `tropCert = log ∘ rowNorm` is **subadditive**
  (`tropCert_mul_le`, `tropCert_wordMatrix_le`) — the tropical/max-plus image of the
  multiplicative bound.

The following conjectures are precise and falsifiable; each is intended to seed a
follow-up Lean formalization.

## Conjecture 1 (Sharpness of the tropical depth bound)
The `7^d` certificate is tight up to the constant: for the all-`B` word `Bᵈ`, the
hypotenuse of the resulting triple satisfies `c ≥ 5·5^d` and `c ≤ 5·7^d`, and the
ratio `log c / d → log r` for some `r ∈ [5,7]`. **Sharper claim:** `r = 1+2√2`
(the spectral radius / dominant eigenvalue of `matB`), i.e.
`lim_{d→∞} (1/d)·tropCert(Bᵈ) = log(1+2√2)`. Falsifiable by computing `rowNorm(Bᵈ)`
growth vs. `(1+2√2)^d`.

## Conjecture 2 (Spectral-radius refinement of `rowNorm`)
For every Berggren word matrix `M = wordMatrix w`, the *exact* asymptotic growth of
`rowNorm(Mᵏ)` as `k→∞` is governed by the Perron eigenvalue `λ(M)` of `|M|`, giving a
strengthened certificate `tropCert(Mᵏ) = k·log λ(M) + O(1)`. This would replace the
uniform constant `log 7` by a per-word Lyapunov exponent and is the tropical
linearization of the Berggren dynamics.

## Conjecture 3 (Reduction is the inverse functor and strictly decreases the certificate)
Define the reduction step by the inverse generators `invA, invB, invC` (from Core).
Then for any non-seed primitive triple `v` with hypotenuse `c > 5`, exactly one inverse
generator strictly decreases the hypotenuse, and the induced reduction word `w⁻¹`
satisfies `tropCert(wordMatrix w⁻¹) = tropCert(wordMatrix w)` (the certificate is a
two-sided invariant of the word, not just an upper bound). Equivalently: the Berggren
reduction algorithm terminates in exactly `length(w)` steps, matching the certificate.

## Conjecture 4 (Functorial transfer to ultrametric robustness)
Composing the tropical certificate with the valuation-reconstruction functor of
`Bridges/CategoricalTropicalUltrametric.lean` yields a certified ultrametric Lipschitz
bound: the Berggren action is `7^d`-Lipschitz in the L∞ metric, and the reconstructed
ultrametric seminorm makes it `1`-Lipschitz (an isometry) after rescaling by the
tropical certificate. Falsifiable by exhibiting a triple pair whose ultrametric
distance is *not* preserved.

## Conjecture 5 (Generalization to higher-dimensional Lorentz monoids)
For the O(n-1,1;ℤ) analogue generating Pythagorean (n-1)-tuples, the same L∞ row-norm
certificate holds with uniform generator norm `g(n) = 2n-1` (so `g(3)=7`). The
functorial tropical bound becomes depth `≥ log_{2n-1}(c/seed)`. Falsifiable by
constructing the n=4 generators (quadruples `a²+b²+c²=d²`) and checking
`rowNorm = 9` uniformly.

formalization in `Catalog.Algebra.BerggrenLorentz.Core`.

coordinate.  On triples in *standard position* (positive legs, hypotenuse
largest) this is exactly the hypotenuse `c`, and the three Berggren generators
act on it by the explicit affine forms

* `T (childA x) = 2a - 2b + 3c`,
* `T (childB x) = 2a + 2b + 3c`,
* `T (childC x) = -2a + 2b + 3c`,

which are precisely the third rows `hypA`, `hypB`, `hypC` of the generators.

* `tropHeight_childA_grow / B / C` and `T_step_grow` : every child strictly
  increases `T`, in fact by at least `2`; `T_step_mono` records monotonicity.
* `applyWord_ordered` : standard position is preserved along the whole tree.
* `T_applyWord_lower` : along any word `w` of generators, the tropical height

namespace BerggrenLorentz.Tropical

open BerggrenLorentz

/-! ## Section 1: The tropical height and the standard-position region -/

/-- The **tropical height** of a triple: the max-plus linear form picking out the
largest coordinate, `T(a,b,c) = max (max a b) c`. Explicit and computable. -/
def tropHeight (a b c : ℤ) : ℤ := max (max a b) c

/-- The **standard-position region**: positive coordinates with the third
coordinate (the hypotenuse) at least as large as both legs.  Every primitive
Pythagorean triple with positive legs lies here. -/
def Ordered (a b c : ℤ) : Prop := 0 < a ∧ 0 < b ∧ 0 < c ∧ a ≤ c ∧ b ≤ c

/-- Primitive Pythagorean triples with positive entries lie in standard position. -/
theorem ordered_of_pythag (a b c : ℤ) (h : IsPythag a b c)
    (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hc : 0 < c) : Ordered a b c :=
  ⟨ha, hb, hc, by nlinarith only [ha, hb, hc, h.symm], by nlinarith only [ha, hb, hc, h.symm]⟩

/-- On standard-position triples the tropical height is exactly the hypotenuse. -/
theorem tropHeight_eq_hyp (a b c : ℤ) (h : Ordered a b c) :
    tropHeight a b c = c :=
  max_eq_right (max_le h.2.2.2.1 h.2.2.2.2)

/-! ## Section 2: Closure of standard position under the Berggren children -/

/-- The A-child of a standard-position triple is again in standard position. -/
theorem ordered_childA (a b c : ℤ) (h : Ordered a b c) :
    Ordered (childA a b c).1 (childA a b c).2.1 (childA a b c).2.2 := by
  obtain ⟨ha, hb, hc, hab, hbc⟩ := h
  constructor <;> norm_num [childA] <;> omega

/-- The B-child of a standard-position triple is again in standard position. -/
theorem ordered_childB (a b c : ℤ) (h : Ordered a b c) :
    Ordered (childB a b c).1 (childB a b c).2.1 (childB a b c).2.2 := by
  obtain ⟨ha, hb, hc, hac, hbc⟩ := h
  constructor <;> norm_num [childB] <;> omega

/-- The C-child of a standard-position triple is again in standard position. -/
theorem ordered_childC (a b c : ℤ) (h : Ordered a b c) :
    Ordered (childC a b c).1 (childC a b c).2.1 (childC a b c).2.2 := by
  obtain ⟨ha, hb, hc, h₁, h₂⟩ := h
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩ <;> · unfold childC; norm_num; omega

/-! ## Section 3: Exact tropical recursion formulas for the three children -/

/-- Tropical recursion along the A-branch: `T (childA x) = 2a - 2b + 3c`
(the `hypA` row). -/
theorem tropHeight_childA (a b c : ℤ) (h : Ordered a b c) :
    tropHeight (childA a b c).1 (childA a b c).2.1 (childA a b c).2.2
      = 2*a - 2*b + 3*c := by
  unfold tropHeight childA
  grind +locals

/-- Tropical recursion along the B-branch: `T (childB x) = 2a + 2b + 3c`
(the `hypB` row). -/
theorem tropHeight_childB (a b c : ℤ) (h : Ordered a b c) :
    tropHeight (childB a b c).1 (childB a b c).2.1 (childB a b c).2.2
      = 2*a + 2*b + 3*c := by
  unfold tropHeight childB
  grind +locals

/-- Tropical recursion along the C-branch: `T (childC x) = -2a + 2b + 3c`
(the `hypC` row). -/
theorem tropHeight_childC (a b c : ℤ) (h : Ordered a b c) :
    tropHeight (childC a b c).1 (childC a b c).2.1 (childC a b c).2.2
      = -2*a + 2*b + 3*c := by
  unfold tropHeight childC
  grind +locals

/-! ## Section 4: Strict tropical growth (monotonicity) for each child -/

/-- The A-child strictly increases the tropical height, by at least `2`. -/
theorem tropHeight_childA_grow (a b c : ℤ) (h : Ordered a b c) :
    tropHeight a b c + 2
      ≤ tropHeight (childA a b c).1 (childA a b c).2.1 (childA a b c).2.2 := by
  obtain ⟨ha, hb, hc, hab, hbc⟩ := h
  unfold tropHeight childA
  grind

/-- The B-child strictly increases the tropical height, by at least `2`. -/
theorem tropHeight_childB_grow (a b c : ℤ) (h : Ordered a b c) :
    tropHeight a b c + 2
      ≤ tropHeight (childB a b c).1 (childB a b c).2.1 (childB a b c).2.2 := by
  unfold tropHeight childB
  grind +locals

/-- The C-child strictly increases the tropical height, by at least `2`. -/
theorem tropHeight_childC_grow (a b c : ℤ) (h : Ordered a b c) :
    tropHeight a b c + 2
      ≤ tropHeight (childC a b c).1 (childC a b c).2.1 (childC a b c).2.2 := by
  unfold tropHeight childC at *
  grind +locals

/-! ## Section 5: The Berggren dynamics on triples and words -/

/-- One Berggren step indexed by a generator `k : Fin 3`. -/
def step : Fin 3 → ℤ × ℤ × ℤ → ℤ × ℤ × ℤ
  | 0, t => childA t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2
  | 1, t => childB t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2
  | 2, t => childC t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2

/-- The tropical height as a function on triples. -/
def T (t : ℤ × ℤ × ℤ) : ℤ := tropHeight t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2

/-- Standard position as a predicate on triples. -/
def OrderedT (t : ℤ × ℤ × ℤ) : Prop := Ordered t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2

/-- Apply a word of Berggren generators, reading letters left to right. -/
def applyWord (w : List (Fin 3)) (t : ℤ × ℤ × ℤ) : ℤ × ℤ × ℤ :=
  w.foldl (fun acc k => step k acc) t

/-- A single Berggren step preserves standard position. -/
theorem ordered_step (k : Fin 3) (t : ℤ × ℤ × ℤ) (h : OrderedT t) :
    OrderedT (step k t) := by
  fin_cases k <;> simp_all +decide [OrderedT]
  · exact ordered_childA _ _ _ h
  · exact ordered_childB _ _ _ h
  · exact ordered_childC _ _ _ h

/-- A single Berggren step increases the tropical height by at least `2`. -/
theorem T_step_grow (k : Fin 3) (t : ℤ × ℤ × ℤ) (h : OrderedT t) :
    T t + 2 ≤ T (step k t) := by
  fin_cases k <;> simp +decide [T, OrderedT] at *
  · exact tropHeight_childA_grow _ _ _ h
  · convert tropHeight_childB_grow t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2 h using 1
  · convert tropHeight_childC_grow t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2 h using 1

/-- Monotonicity: every Berggren child has tropical height at least that of its
parent. -/
theorem T_step_mono (k : Fin 3) (t : ℤ × ℤ × ℤ) (h : OrderedT t) :
    T t ≤ T (step k t) := by
  have := T_step_grow k t h
  omega

/-! ## Section 6: The path-growth theorem along a word -/

/-- Standard position is preserved along an arbitrary word of generators,
so the whole Berggren tree stays in the region where `T` is the hypotenuse. -/
theorem applyWord_ordered (w : List (Fin 3)) (t : ℤ × ℤ × ℤ) (h : OrderedT t) :
    OrderedT (applyWord w t) := by
  induction w generalizing t with
  | nil => simpa [applyWord] using h
  | cons k w ih => exact ih (step k t) (ordered_step k t h)

/-- **Path-growth theorem.** Along any word `w` of Berggren generators, the
tropical height grows at least linearly in the depth:
`T (applyWord w x) ≥ T x + 2 * |w|`. -/
theorem T_applyWord_lower (w : List (Fin 3)) (t : ℤ × ℤ × ℤ) (h : OrderedT t) :
    T t + 2 * (w.length : ℤ) ≤ T (applyWord w t) := by
  induction w generalizing t with
  | nil => simp [applyWord]
  | cons k w ih =>
    have hstep := T_step_grow k t h
    have hih := ih (step k t) (ordered_step k t h)
    simp only [applyWord, List.foldl_cons, List.length_cons] at *
    push_cast
    linarith

/-! ## Section 7: Executable evaluation and concrete instances -/

/-- The Berggren seed triple `(3,4,5)`. -/
def seed : ℤ × ℤ × ℤ := (3, 4, 5)

/-- The seed is in standard position. -/
theorem ordered_seed : OrderedT seed := by
  unfold OrderedT Ordered seed
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩ <;> decide

/-- Concrete evaluation: three B-steps from the seed reach `(697, 696, 985)`. -/
theorem applyWord_BBB : applyWord [1, 1, 1] seed = (697, 696, 985) := by
  unfold applyWord seed
  decide

/-- Concrete tropical height after three B-steps. -/
theorem T_applyWord_BBB : T (applyWord [1, 1, 1] seed) = 985 := by
  rw [applyWord_BBB]; decide

/-- The path-growth bound, instantiated at the seed and the word `BBB`:
the tropical height grows by at least `6` over three steps (here it grows from
`5` to `985`). -/
theorem T_seed_BBB_lower :
    T seed + 2 * (([1, 1, 1] : List (Fin 3)).length : ℤ) ≤ T (applyWord [1, 1, 1] seed) :=
  T_applyWord_lower [1, 1, 1] seed ordered_seed

# The Markov Basis Theorem for the Two-Way Independence Model

This file gives a self-contained formalization of the classical theorem from
algebraic statistics that the set of basic `2 × 2` swap moves

  `B(i,i',j,j') = e_{i,j'} + e_{i',j} - e_{i,j} - e_{i',j'}`   (`i ≠ i'`, `j ≠ j'`)

is a *Markov basis* for the two-way independence model: any two nonnegative
contingency tables with the same row and column margins are connected by a finite
sequence of these moves that stays inside the nonnegative fiber.

## Main definitions

* `Table m n`         — integer contingency tables on `Fin m × Fin n`.
* `rowSum`, `colSum`  — the row and column margins.
* `SameMargins u v`   — `u` and `v` have equal row sums and equal column sums.
* `Nonneg u`          — all entries of `u` are `≥ 0`.
* `basicMove i i' j j'`— the basic `2 × 2` move with the standard `±1` pattern.
* `Step u v`          — one oriented move between two nonnegative tables.
* `tdist u v`         — the `ℓ¹` distance `∑ |u i j - v i j|`.

## Main results

* `basicMove_preserves_rowSums`, `basicMove_preserves_colSums`,
  `basicMove_preserves_margins`, `Step.preserve_margins` — margin invariance.
* `exists_sign_rectangle` — the combinatorial extraction lemma: a nonzero
  difference with zero margins contains a sign-changing `2 × 2` rectangle.
* `exists_reducing_step` — distance reduction: an oriented move strictly
  decreasing the `ℓ¹` distance while staying nonnegative.
* `twoWay_fiber_connected` — the Markov basis theorem: connectivity of the
  nonnegative fiber via `Relation.ReflTransGen Step`.

import Mathlib

open scoped BigOperators

namespace TwoWayMarkov

/-- An integer-valued contingency table on `Fin m × Fin n`. -/
abbrev Table (m n : ℕ) := Fin m → Fin n → ℤ

variable {m n : ℕ}

/-- The `i`-th row margin. -/
def rowSum (u : Table m n) (i : Fin m) : ℤ := ∑ j, u i j

/-- The `j`-th column margin. -/
def colSum (u : Table m n) (j : Fin n) : ℤ := ∑ i, u i j

/-- Two tables lie in the same fiber: they have equal row and column margins. -/
def SameMargins (u v : Table m n) : Prop :=
  (∀ i, rowSum u i = rowSum v i) ∧ (∀ j, colSum u j = colSum v j)

/-- A table is nonnegative if all of its entries are `≥ 0`. -/
def Nonneg (u : Table m n) : Prop := ∀ i j, 0 ≤ u i j

/-- The basic `2 × 2` move `B(i,i',j,j') = e_{i,j'} + e_{i',j} - e_{i,j} - e_{i',j'}`. -/
def basicMove (i i' : Fin m) (j j' : Fin n) : Table m n := fun a b =>
  (if a = i ∧ b = j' then 1 else 0)
    + (if a = i' ∧ b = j then 1 else 0)
    - (if a = i ∧ b = j then 1 else 0)
    - (if a = i' ∧ b = j' then 1 else 0)

/-- One oriented basic move between two nonnegative tables in the same fiber. -/
def Step (u v : Table m n) : Prop :=
  Nonneg u ∧ Nonneg v ∧ ∃ (i i' : Fin m) (j j' : Fin n),
    i ≠ i' ∧ j ≠ j' ∧ (v = u + basicMove i i' j j' ∨ v = u - basicMove i i' j j')

/-! ### Basic arithmetic of margins -/

theorem rowSum_add (u v : Table m n) (i : Fin m) :
    rowSum (u + v) i = rowSum u i + rowSum v i := by
  exact Finset.sum_add_distrib

theorem colSum_add (u v : Table m n) (j : Fin n) :
    colSum (u + v) j = colSum u j + colSum v j := by
  exact Finset.sum_add_distrib

theorem rowSum_sub (u v : Table m n) (i : Fin m) :
    rowSum (u - v) i = rowSum u i - rowSum v i := by
  simp only [rowSum, Pi.sub_apply, Finset.sum_sub_distrib]

theorem colSum_sub (u v : Table m n) (j : Fin n) :
    colSum (u - v) j = colSum u j - colSum v j := by
  simp only [colSum, Pi.sub_apply, Finset.sum_sub_distrib]

  split_ifs <;> ring

/-! ### The combinatorial extraction lemma -/

/-- If a finite sum of integers is zero and one term is positive, some term is negative. -/
theorem exists_neg_of_pos_sum_zero {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (f : ι → ℤ)
    (hsum : ∑ i, f i = 0) (a : ι) (hpos : 0 < f a) : ∃ b, f b < 0 := by

  exact absurd hsum ( ne_of_gt ( lt_of_lt_of_le hpos ( Finset.single_le_sum ( fun i _ => h i ) ( Finset.mem_univ a ) ) ) )

    ∃ (i i' : Fin m) (j j' : Fin n),

Solutions descend from `N` to any divisor `M`: if `M ∣ N` and
`a^x + b^y = c^z` has unit solutions in `ZMod N`, then it has
unit solutions in `ZMod M`.
-/
theorem primitiveResidueSolution_of_dvd
    {M N x y z : ℕ}
    (hdvd : M ∣ N)
    (hsol : PrimitiveResidueSolution N x y z) :
    PrimitiveResidueSolution M x y z := by
  rcases hsol with ⟨ a, b, c, ha, hb, hc, h ⟩;
  -- Use the ring homomorphism `ZMod.castHom hdvd (ZMod M) : ZMod N →+* ZMod M`.
  set f : ZMod N →+* ZMod M := ZMod.castHom hdvd (ZMod M);
  exact ⟨ f a, f b, f c, ha.map f, hb.map f, hc.map f, by simpa using congr_arg f h ⟩

/-- **Obstruction Monotonicity**: if no primitive residue solution exists
mod M, then none exists mod any multiple of M. One obstructing modulus
annihilates all its multiples. -/
theorem no_primitiveResidueSolution_of_dvd
    {M N x y z : ℕ}
    (hdvd : M ∣ N)
    (hno : ¬ PrimitiveResidueSolution M x y z) :
    ¬ PrimitiveResidueSolution N x y z :=
  fun hsol => hno (primitiveResidueSolution_of_dvd hdvd hsol)

# Future Directions — Discrete Hodge Laplacian, Harmonic Space & Diffusion Message Passing

## Synthesis

This cycle rebuilds the discrete Hodge program on a **self-contained Mathlib foundation**.
The previous catalog `Hodge*` stack did not elaborate: `HodgeMessagePassingConvergence`
imports a module `Speculative.AutoResearch.HodgeSpectralThreshold` that does not exist in the
repository, and the package declared no `srcDir`, so `lake` could not even locate the catalog
sources. Two infrastructure repairs were made — adding `srcDir = "Catalog"` to `lakefile.toml`
so module resolution works at all — and a new, dependency-free file
`Catalog/Speculative/AutoResearch/HodgeLaplacianGreen.lean` re-derives the operator-algebra,
analytic, and dynamical layers of the program from Mathlib alone.

The central object is the discrete **Hodge Laplacian** of a two-step cochain complex of
finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces

```
U --e--> V --d--> W ,        Δ = d* ∘ d + e ∘ e*   on   V ,
```

with `d* = LinearMap.adjoint d` and `e* = LinearMap.adjoint e`. The single organizing identity
is the sum-of-squares **Dirichlet energy**

```
⟪Δ x, x⟫ = ‖d x‖² + ‖e* x‖² ,
```

from which everything else follows. The harmonic space `ker Δ` is exactly the
closed-and-co-closed cochains (`d x = 0 ∧ e* x = 0`); the Rayleigh form is strictly positive
off `ker Δ`; self-adjointness places the image of `Δ` inside `(ker Δ)ᗮ`. On the dynamical
side, the explicit-Euler diffusion step `S = id − a·Δ` fixes the harmonic space pointwise and
conserves the harmonic projection along the whole trajectory, `P (Sᵏ x) = P x`: diffusion
never creates or destroys the topological (harmonic) component, it only relaxes the
exact / co-exact part. This is the local-to-global picture made discrete: local data (the maps
`d`, `e` on individual cochains) glues, via the Hodge decomposition, into the global
obstruction object `ker Δ`.

## Results summary (proved sorry-free; axioms `propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound`)

| Theorem | Statement |
|---|---|
| `hodgeLap_isSymmetric` | `Δ` is self-adjoint |
| `hodgeLap_quadratic_form` | `⟪Δ x, x⟫ = ‖d x‖² + ‖e* x‖²` |
| `hodgeLap_apply_eq_zero_iff` | `Δ x = 0 ↔ d x = 0 ∧ e* x = 0` (harmonic ⇔ closed & co-closed) |
| `hodgeLap_quadratic_eq_zero_iff` | `⟪Δ x, x⟫ = 0 ↔ Δ x = 0` (strict positivity off the kernel) |
| `hodgeLap_apply_mem_orthogonal_ker` | `Δ x ∈ (ker Δ)ᗮ` |
| `diffStep_harmonic_fixed` / `diffStep_pow_harmonic_fixed` | `Sᵏ h = h` for harmonic `h` |
| `harmonicProjection_diffStep` / `harmonicProjection_diffStep_pow` | `P (Sᵏ x) = P x` |

## Research directions

### 1. From "image in `(ker Δ)ᗮ`" to the orthogonal splitting `range Δ = (ker Δ)ᗮ`
This cycle proves the easy inclusion `Δ x ∈ (ker Δ)ᗮ` (`hodgeLap_apply_mem_orthogonal_ker`).
Conjecture the full identity `range Δ = (ker Δ)ᗮ`, and consequently that `Δ` is a linear
isomorphism of `(ker Δ)ᗮ` onto itself. Falsifiable by any `y ∈ (ker Δ)ᗮ` not of the form
`Δ x`, or any nonzero `z ∈ (ker Δ)ᗮ` with `Δ z = 0`. **The key insight is** that injectivity
on the complement is immediate from strict positivity — if `z ∈ (ker Δ)ᗮ` and `Δ z = 0` then
`z ∈ ker Δ ∩ (ker Δ)ᗮ = 0` — and in finite dimensions an injective self-map of `(ker Δ)ᗮ` is
surjective, so the rank–nullity count `dim(range Δ) = dim V − dim(ker Δ) = dim (ker Δ)ᗮ`
closes the inclusion to an equality. **Why now?** Self-adjointness, strict positivity, and the
membership lemma are all theorems this cycle, so the remaining step is a dimension count using
Mathlib's `LinearMap.finrank_range_add_finrank_ker` and `Submodule.finrank_add_finrank_orthogonal`.

### 2. Bundle the Green's operator into an honest self-adjoint linear map
With Direction 1 in hand, every `x` has a unique `z ∈ (ker Δ)ᗮ` with `Δ z = x − P x`.
Conjecture this assembles into a genuine `G : V →ₗ[ℝ] V` with `Δ ∘ G = G ∘ Δ = id − P`,
`G ∘ P = 0`, and `G` self-adjoint (`⟪G x, y⟫ = ⟪x, G y⟫`). Falsifiable by a candidate `G` with
`Δ (G x) ≠ x − P x` on some `x`, or with `⟪G x, y⟫ ≠ ⟪x, G y⟫`. **The key insight is** that
uniqueness is the *only* obstruction to linearity of a solver: `z(x+y)` and `z(x)+z(y)` solve
the same problem, so injectivity on `(ker Δ)ᗮ` forces them equal, making
`G x := Classical.choose …` automatically additive and homogeneous, with `LinearMap.mk` closing
the construction. **Why now?** Direction 1 supplies the existence-and-uniqueness needed; each
`LinearMap` axiom is then a one-line uniqueness argument, and self-adjointness follows from
`hodgeLap_isSymmetric` restricted to the invariant complement.

### 3. The diffusion energy is a strict Lyapunov function with harmonic limit
Conjecture the Dirichlet energy `E(x) = ⟪Δ x, x⟫` is non-increasing along admissible diffusion,
`E(S x) ≤ E(x)` for `0 < a < 2/λ_max`, with equality iff `x` is harmonic, and that `Sᵏ x → P x`
as `k → ∞`. Falsifiable by an `x` and admissible `a` with `E(S x) > E(x)`, or a non-harmonic
fixed point of `S`. **The key insight is** that `hodgeLap_quadratic_form` already exhibits `E`
as a sum of squares whose zero set is exactly `ker Δ` (`hodgeLap_quadratic_eq_zero_iff`), and
`harmonicProjection_diffStep_pow` pins the limit's harmonic part to `P x`, so only the
complementary part must be shown to vanish. **Why now?** Both the Lyapunov candidate (the proven
quadratic form) and the conserved target (`P x`) are in hand; monotonicity reduces to the single
algebraic estimate `E(x) − E(Sx) = 2a⟪Δx,Δx⟫ − a²⟪Δx,Δ(Δx)⟫ ≥ 0` once `Δ` is bounded by `λ_max`
on the complement.

### 4. Spectral resolution `Δ = Σ λᵢ Pᵢ` with `P₀ = P` and `G = Σ_{λᵢ>0} λᵢ⁻¹ Pᵢ`
Conjecture the finite-dimensional spectral theorem for `Δ`: an orthonormal eigenbasis with
`0 = λ₀ ≤ λ₁ ≤ …`, the `0`-eigenprojection equal to the harmonic projection `P`, `Δ = Σ λᵢ Pᵢ`,
and the Green's operator of Direction 2 equal to `G = Σ_{λᵢ>0} λᵢ⁻¹ Pᵢ`. Falsifiable by a
negative eigenvalue, a non-harmonic `0`-eigenvector, or a mismatch `G ≠ Σ λᵢ⁻¹ Pᵢ`. **The key
insight is** that `hodgeLap_isSymmetric` feeds Mathlib's finite-dimensional spectral theorem
directly, the quadratic form pins the spectrum to `[0, ∞)`, and `hodgeLap_quadratic_eq_zero_iff`
identifies the `0`-eigenspace with `ker Δ`, so the eigendecomposition is an *application* rather
than a new theory. **Why now?** All three hypotheses of the spectral theorem are theorems this
cycle, and Direction 2's Green operator forces the inverse-eigenvalue formula once the
eigenprojections exist; the contraction rate `ρ = max_{λ>0} |1 − aλ|` of diffusion then drops out
per eigenvector.

### 5. The discrete Hodge isomorphism `ker d / range e ≃ ker Δ` as a quotient isometry
Conjecture that the harmonic representative realizes the cohomology quotient: every closed class
`[x]` (with `d x = 0`) has a unique harmonic representative `P x ∈ ker Δ`, giving a linear
isomorphism `ker d / range e ≃ ker Δ` that is moreover an **isometry** for the quotient norm,
`‖[x]‖ = ‖P x‖`. (This direction needs the cochain condition `d ∘ e = 0`, which the present file
does not yet assume.) Falsifiable by a closed `x` whose harmonic projection leaves the class, or a
class whose quotient norm differs from `‖P x‖`. **The key insight is** that Direction 1's splitting
`range Δ = (ker Δ)ᗮ` separates any closed cochain into a harmonic part `P x` and a part in
`range Δ = range d* ⊕ range e`; restricted to closed cochains the `d*`-component vanishes, so
`x − P x ∈ range e` and `P x` is the canonical representative, with `‖P x‖ ≤ ‖x − e u‖` making the
quotient infimum attained exactly at `P x`. **Why now?** The orthogonal splitting and harmonic
projection identities are (or shortly will be) theorems; only the identification of Mathlib's
`Submodule.Quotient.norm_mk` infimum with this attained minimum remains to upgrade the linear iso
to a `LinearIsometryEquiv`.

import Mathlib

/-!
# Markov bases for two-way contingency tables

This file develops a small algebraic foundation for the Markov basis of two-way
contingency tables with fixed row and column margins.

A `Table m n` is an integer matrix.  The fundamental *basic move* adds `±1` to the
four corners of a `2 × 2` sub-rectangle, an operation that preserves all row and
column sums.  We record this fact together with the additivity needed to show that
a legal basic step between two non-negative tables preserves the margins.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MarkovBases.TwoWay

/-- An integer-valued two-way table. -/
abbrev Table (m n : ℕ) := Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℤ

variable {m n : ℕ}

/-- The sum of the entries in row `i`. -/
def rowSum (T : Table m n) (i : Fin m) : ℤ := ∑ j, T i j

/-- The sum of the entries in column `j`. -/
def colSum (T : Table m n) (j : Fin n) : ℤ := ∑ i, T i j

/-- The sum of all entries of the table. -/
def totalSum (T : Table m n) : ℤ := ∑ i, ∑ j, T i j

/-- Two tables have the same margins when their row sums and column sums agree. -/
def sameMargins (T₁ T₂ : Table m n) : Prop :=
  (∀ i, rowSum T₁ i = rowSum T₂ i) ∧ (∀ j, colSum T₁ j = colSum T₂ j)

/-- The basic move on the `2 × 2` sub-rectangle with rows `i, i'` and columns `j, j'`:
it places `+1` at `(i, j')` and `(i', j)`, `-1` at `(i, j)` and `(i', j')`, and `0`
elsewhere. -/
def basicMove (i i' : Fin m) (j j' : Fin n) (_hii' : i ≠ i') (_hjj' : j ≠ j') :
    Table m n :=
  fun a b =>
    if a = i ∧ b = j' then 1
    else if a = i' ∧ b = j then 1
    else if a = i ∧ b = j then -1
    else if a = i' ∧ b = j' then -1
    else 0

/-- A table is non-negative when all of its entries are. -/
def Nonneg (T : Table m n) : Prop := ∀ i j, 0 ≤ T i j

/-- `T'` is obtained from `T` by a legal basic step: a basic move that keeps both
tables non-negative. -/
def LegalBasicStep (T T' : Table m n) : Prop :=
  ∃ (i i' : Fin m) (j j' : Fin n) (hii' : i ≠ i') (hjj' : j ≠ j'),
    T' = T + basicMove i i' j j' hii' hjj' ∧ Nonneg T ∧ Nonneg T'

/-- Each row sum of a basic move is zero. -/
lemma basicMove_rowSum_zero (i i' : Fin m) (j j' : Fin n) (hii' : i ≠ i')
    (hjj' : j ≠ j') (k : Fin m) :
    rowSum (basicMove i i' j j' hii' hjj') k = 0 := by
  by_cases hi : k = i <;> by_cases hi' : k = i' <;> simp_all +decide [ rowSum ];
  · grind;
  · simp +decide [ basicMove, Finset.sum_ite ];
    simp_all +decide [ Finset.filter_eq', Finset.filter_ne' ];
  · simp +decide [ basicMove ];
    simp +decide [ Finset.sum_ite, hi ];
    rw [ Finset.card_filter ] ; aesop;
  · unfold basicMove; aesop;

/-- Each column sum of a basic move is zero. -/
lemma basicMove_colSum_zero (i i' : Fin m) (j j' : Fin n) (hii' : i ≠ i')
    (hjj' : j ≠ j') (l : Fin n) :
    colSum (basicMove i i' j j' hii' hjj') l = 0 := by
  convert basicMove_rowSum_zero j j' i i' hjj' hii' l using 1;
  convert rfl using 2;
  ext; simp +decide [ rowSum, colSum, basicMove ] ;
  grind

/-- A basic move preserves margins: it has the same margins as the zero table. -/
lemma basicMove_preserves_margins (i i' : Fin m) (j j' : Fin n) (hii' : i ≠ i')
    (hjj' : j ≠ j') :
    sameMargins (basicMove i i' j j' hii' hjj') (0 : Table m n) := by
  constructor <;> intro k <;> simp_all +decide [ basicMove_rowSum_zero, basicMove_colSum_zero ];
  · exact Eq.symm ( Finset.sum_eq_zero fun _ _ => rfl );
  · unfold colSum; aesop;

open Classical
open Bridges.AlgebraMachineLearning

namespace Bridges.NeuralProofSpectrum

universe u v w

variable {R S T K : Type*} {α : Type*}

/-! ## Section 1: Identity and composition of algebraic neural morphisms

`AlgNeuralHom` morphisms form a category: the identity state map intertwines the dynamics
trivially, and intertwining maps compose.  These are the data needed to phrase the functor
laws below. -/

/-- The identity morphism of an algebraic neural system. -/
def AlgNeuralHom.id [Semiring R] [Semiring K] (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) :
    AlgNeuralHom N N where
  toFun := _root_.id
  map_step := fun _ _ => rfl
  map_observe := fun _ => rfl

@[simp] theorem AlgNeuralHom.id_toFun [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) : (AlgNeuralHom.id N).toFun = _root_.id := rfl

/-- Composition of morphisms of algebraic neural systems. -/
def AlgNeuralHom.comp [Semiring R] [Semiring S] [Semiring T] [Semiring K]
    {N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α} {M : AlgNeuralSystem S K α} {P : AlgNeuralSystem T K α}
    (f : AlgNeuralHom N M) (g : AlgNeuralHom M P) : AlgNeuralHom N P where
  toFun := g.toFun ∘ f.toFun
  map_step := fun x a => by
    simp only [Function.comp_apply]
    rw [f.map_step, g.map_step]
  map_observe := fun x => (f.map_observe x).trans (g.map_observe (f.toFun x))

@[simp] theorem AlgNeuralHom.comp_toFun [Semiring R] [Semiring S] [Semiring T] [Semiring K]
    {N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α} {M : AlgNeuralSystem S K α} {P : AlgNeuralSystem T K α}
    (f : AlgNeuralHom N M) (g : AlgNeuralHom M P) :
    (f.comp g).toFun = g.toFun ∘ f.toFun := rfl

/-! ## Section 2: Functor laws on the behavior map -/

/-- **Identity law (behavior).** The identity morphism does not change behavior. -/
theorem algBehavior_map_id [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (x : R) (w : List α) :
    algBehavior N ((AlgNeuralHom.id N).toFun x) w = algBehavior N x w := rfl

/-- **Composition law (behavior).** Behavior is transported along a composite morphism by
    transporting along its two factors in turn. -/
theorem algBehavior_map_comp [Semiring R] [Semiring S] [Semiring T] [Semiring K]
    {N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α} {M : AlgNeuralSystem S K α} {P : AlgNeuralSystem T K α}
    (f : AlgNeuralHom N M) (g : AlgNeuralHom M P) (x : R) (w : List α) :
    algBehavior N x w = algBehavior P ((f.comp g).toFun x) w := by
  rw [algBehavior_map f x w, algBehavior_map g (f.toFun x) w]
  rfl

/-! ## Section 3: Functor laws on the proof-spectrum congruence

The assignment `N ↦ behaviorCongruence N` is functorial: identity morphisms act as the
identity on the congruence relation, and the pushforward along a composite equals the
composite of the pushforwards. -/

/-- **Identity law (congruence).** Pushing the congruence forward along the identity
    morphism is the identity on the relation. -/
theorem behaviorCongruence_map_id [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (x y : R) :
    (behaviorCongruence N).rel ((AlgNeuralHom.id N).toFun x) ((AlgNeuralHom.id N).toFun y)
      ↔ (behaviorCongruence N).rel x y := Iff.rfl

/-- **Composition law (congruence).** The pushforward of the congruence along a composite
    morphism factors as the two successive pushforwards. -/
theorem behaviorCongruence_map_comp [Semiring R] [Semiring S] [Semiring T] [Semiring K]
    {N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α} {M : AlgNeuralSystem S K α} {P : AlgNeuralSystem T K α}
    (f : AlgNeuralHom N M) (g : AlgNeuralHom M P) {x y : R}
    (h : (behaviorCongruence N).rel x y) :
    (behaviorCongruence P).rel ((f.comp g).toFun x) ((f.comp g).toFun y) :=
  behaviorCongruence_map g (behaviorCongruence_map f h)

/-! ## Section 4: Prime congruence under a detecting context

The base file's "Failure analysis F2" notes that `behaviorCongruence N` is **not** prime in
general, even when `K` has no zero divisors, because the pointwise disjunction
`∀ w, b a w = 0 ∨ b b w = 0` does not factor.  The clean fix is to assume a *single*
context `w₀` that already detects behavioral equivalence; then the disjunction is decided at
`w₀` and primality follows.  This hypothesis is genuinely used in the proof. -/

/-- `DetectsBehavior N w₀` says the single context `w₀` separates all states: two states are
    behaviorally equivalent iff their observations on `w₀` agree.  (For example, in a
    finite-memory system a sufficiently long universal probing word has this property.) -/
def DetectsBehavior [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (w₀ : List α) : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : R, behaviorRel N x y ↔ algBehavior N x w₀ = algBehavior N y w₀

/-- With a detecting context, vanishing in the congruence is detected at `w₀`. -/
theorem behaviorRel_zero_iff_of_detects [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    {N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α} {w₀ : List α} (h : DetectsBehavior N w₀) (x : R) :
    behaviorRel N x 0 ↔ algBehavior N x w₀ = 0 := by
  rw [h x 0, algBehavior_zero]

/-- **The prime refinement.** If the output semiring has no zero divisors and a single
    context `w₀` detects behavioral equivalence, then the behavior congruence is a *prime*
    semiring congruence — a point of the proof spectrum `ProofSpectrum R`. -/
def behaviorPrimeCongruence [Semiring R] [Semiring K] [NoZeroDivisors K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (w₀ : List α) (h : DetectsBehavior N w₀) :
    PrimeSRCong R :=
  { behaviorCongruence N with
    prime_prop := by
      intro a b hab
      have h0 : algBehavior N (a * b) w₀ = 0 :=
        (behaviorRel_zero_iff_of_detects h (a * b)).mp hab
      rw [algBehavior_mul] at h0
      rcases mul_eq_zero.mp h0 with ha | hb
      · exact Or.inl ((behaviorRel_zero_iff_of_detects h a).mpr ha)
      · exact Or.inr ((behaviorRel_zero_iff_of_detects h b).mpr hb) }

/-- The prime refinement has the expected underlying relation. -/
theorem behaviorPrimeCongruence_rel [Semiring R] [Semiring K] [NoZeroDivisors K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (w₀ : List α) (h : DetectsBehavior N w₀) (x y : R) :
    (behaviorPrimeCongruence N w₀ h).rel x y ↔ (behaviorCongruence N).rel x y := Iff.rfl

/-! ## Section 5: The descended metric on the Myhill–Nerode quotient

The observation pseudometric `obsDist` is constant on behavioral-equivalence classes, so it
descends to the Myhill–Nerode quotient
`Quotient (neural_setoid (weighted_to_neural N.toWeighted))` as a genuine *metric*
(distance `0` iff equal). -/

/-- **Well-definedness / compatibility.** `obsDist` is invariant under replacing either
    argument by a behaviorally-equivalent state. -/
theorem obsDist_congr [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) {x x' y y' : R}
    (hx : behaviorRel N x x') (hy : behaviorRel N y y') :
    obsDist N x y = obsDist N x' y' := by
  have hiff : behaviorRel N x y ↔ behaviorRel N x' y' :=
    ⟨fun h => behaviorRel_trans N (behaviorRel_trans N (behaviorRel_symm N hx) h) hy,
     fun h => behaviorRel_trans N (behaviorRel_trans N hx h) (behaviorRel_symm N hy)⟩
  unfold obsDist
  rw [propext hiff]

/-- The observation pseudometric descended to the Myhill–Nerode quotient. -/
def quotObsDist [Semiring R] [Semiring K] (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) :
    Quotient (neural_setoid (weighted_to_neural N.toWeighted)) →
    Quotient (neural_setoid (weighted_to_neural N.toWeighted)) → ℝ :=
  Quotient.lift₂ (obsDist N) (fun _ _ _ _ hx hy => obsDist_congr N hx hy)

@[simp] theorem quotObsDist_mk [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (x y : R) :
    quotObsDist N (Quotient.mk _ x) (Quotient.mk _ y) = obsDist N x y := rfl

/-- **Capstone (quotient metric).** The descended distance is a genuine metric: it vanishes
    exactly on the diagonal of the Myhill–Nerode quotient. -/
theorem quotObsDist_eq_zero_iff [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α)
    (p q : Quotient (neural_setoid (weighted_to_neural N.toWeighted))) :
    quotObsDist N p q = 0 ↔ p = q := by
  refine Quotient.inductionOn₂ p q ?_
  intro x y
  constructor
  · intro h
    exact Quotient.sound ((obsDist_eq_zero_iff N x y).mp (by rwa [quotObsDist_mk] at h))
  · intro h
    rw [quotObsDist_mk]
    exact (obsDist_eq_zero_iff N x y).mpr (Quotient.exact h)

end Bridges.NeuralProofSpectrum

import Mathlib

open Finset BigOperators

/-! ## Cayley–Dirichlet energy (self-contained) -/

/-- The **Cayley–Dirichlet energy** of `f : G → ℝ` with respect to a generator
set `S`: the total squared oscillation across the left-Cayley edges. -/
noncomputable def cayleyDirichletEnergy {G : Type*} [Fintype G] [Group G]
    (S : Finset G) (f : G → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ x : G, ∑ s ∈ S, (f (s * x) - f x) ^ 2

/-- The Cayley–Dirichlet energy of a constant function is zero. -/
theorem cayleyDirichletEnergy_const {G : Type*} [Fintype G] [Group G]
    (S : Finset G) (c : ℝ) :
    cayleyDirichletEnergy S (fun _ => c) = 0 := by
  simp [cayleyDirichletEnergy]

/-! ## Word reachability from generation -/

/-
Any element of the subgroup closure of S is representable as a product
    of elements from the symmetric set S.
-/
theorem word_in_generators_of_mem_closure
    {G : Type*} [Group G]
    (S : Finset G)
    (hSsymm : ∀ g ∈ S, g⁻¹ ∈ S)
    {g : G}
    (hg : g ∈ Subgroup.closure (↑S : Set G)) :
    ∃ l : List G, (∀ s, s ∈ l → s ∈ S) ∧ l.prod = g := by
  refine' Subgroup.closure_induction _ _ _ _ hg;
  · exact fun x hx => ⟨ [ x ], by simpa using hx ⟩;
  · exact ⟨ [ ], by simp +decide ⟩;
  · rintro x y hx hy ⟨ l₁, hl₁, rfl ⟩ ⟨ l₂, hl₂, rfl ⟩ ; exact ⟨ l₁ ++ l₂, by aesop ⟩;
  · rintro x hx ⟨ l, hl, rfl ⟩;
    refine' ⟨ l.reverse.map fun s => s⁻¹, _, _ ⟩ <;> simp_all +decide [ List.prod_inv_reverse ];
    exact fun s hs => by simpa using hSsymm _ ( hl _ hs ) ;

/-
**Theorem 1 (Cayley connectivity from generation)**:
    If S is a symmetric generating set for a finite group G,
    then for any x, y ∈ G there exists a walk in the generators
    connecting x to y. This is the algebraic backbone that converts
    `Subgroup.closure = ⊤` into a path-construction principle.
-/
theorem cayley_connected_of_closure_eq_top
    {G : Type*} [Fintype G] [Group G]
    (S : Finset G)
    (hSsymm : ∀ g ∈ S, g⁻¹ ∈ S)
    (hgen : Subgroup.closure (↑S : Set G) = ⊤) :
    ∀ x y : G, ∃ l : List G,
      (∀ s, s ∈ l → s ∈ S) ∧ l.prod * x = y := by
  intro x y
  obtain ⟨l, hl⟩ := word_in_generators_of_mem_closure S hSsymm (show y * x⁻¹ ∈ Subgroup.closure (S : Set G) from by
                                                                  aesop);
  exact ⟨ l, hl.1, by rw [ hl.2, mul_assoc, inv_mul_cancel, mul_one ] ⟩

/-! ## Dirichlet energy characterization -/

/-
Zero Dirichlet energy implies the function is invariant under
    each generator: f(s·x) = f(x) for all s ∈ S and x ∈ G.
-/
theorem cayleyDirichletEnergy_zero_imp_generator_invariant
    {G : Type*} [Fintype G] [Group G]
    (S : Finset G)
    (f : G → ℝ)
    (hE : cayleyDirichletEnergy S f = 0) :
    ∀ s ∈ S, ∀ x : G, f (s * x) = f x := by
  unfold cayleyDirichletEnergy at hE;
  rw [ Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg fun _ _ => Finset.sum_nonneg fun _ _ => sq_nonneg _ ] at hE;
  simp_all +decide [ Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg, sq_nonneg, sub_eq_zero ]

/-
If f is invariant under each generator of a generating set,
    then f is constant.
-/
theorem constant_of_generator_invariant
    {G : Type*} [Fintype G] [Group G]
    (S : Finset G)
    (hSsymm : ∀ g ∈ S, g⁻¹ ∈ S)
    (hgen : Subgroup.closure (↑S : Set G) = ⊤)
    (f : G → ℝ)
    (hinv : ∀ s ∈ S, ∀ x : G, f (s * x) = f x) :
    ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ x : G, f x = c := by
  -- By `word_in_generators_of_mem_closure`, since `x ∈ closure S`, choose `l : List G`,
  -- `l.prod = x`, `∀ s, s ∈ l → s ∈ S`.
  have h_homogenize : ∀ x : G, ∃ l : List G, (∀ s, s ∈ l → s ∈ S) ∧ l.prod = x := by
    intro x
    apply word_in_generators_of_mem_closure S hSsymm
    exact hgen.symm ▸ Subgroup.mem_top x;
  use f 1;
  intro x; obtain ⟨ l, hlS, rfl ⟩ := h_homogenize x; induction l <;> simp_all +decide ;

/-- **Theorem 2 (Zero-energy characterization)**:
    For a symmetric generating set S of a finite group G,
    the Dirichlet energy E_S(f) = 0 iff f is constant.

    This is the formalized principle that *connectivity kills
    nontrivial harmonic defects*. It is the finite-group analogue
    of ergodicity implying uniqueness of equilibrium. -/
theorem cayleyDirichletEnergy_eq_zero_iff_constant
    {G : Type*} [Fintype G] [Group G]
    (S : Finset G)
    (hSsymm : ∀ g ∈ S, g⁻¹ ∈ S)
    (hgen : Subgroup.closure (↑S : Set G) = ⊤)
    (f : G → ℝ) :
    cayleyDirichletEnergy S f = 0 ↔ ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ x : G, f x = c := by
  constructor
  · intro hE
    exact constant_of_generator_invariant S hSsymm hgen f
      (cayleyDirichletEnergy_zero_imp_generator_invariant S f hE)
  · rintro ⟨c, hc⟩
    have : f = fun _ => c := funext hc
    rw [this]
    exact cayleyDirichletEnergy_const S c

import Mathlib
import Computation.PadicValuationDepth

/-- A `MaxPlusDepthSystem` bundles a composition law on `α` together with a
`Nat`-valued depth obeying the tropical (max-plus) composition inequality. -/
structure MaxPlusDepthSystem (α : Type*) where
  comp : α → α → α
  depth : α → Nat
  depth_comp_le : ∀ f g, depth (comp f g) ≤ max (depth f) (depth g) + 1

namespace MaxPlusDepthSystem

variable {α : Type*}

/-- The multiplicative *shadow* of `f` at base `b`: exponentiate the depth. -/
def shadow (S : MaxPlusDepthSystem α) (b : Nat) (f : α) : Nat := b ^ S.depth f

/-- Iterated self-composition: `iter (n+1) f = comp (iter n f) f`. -/
def iter (S : MaxPlusDepthSystem α) : Nat → α → α
  | 0, f => f
  | n + 1, f => S.comp (iter S n f) f

@[simp]
theorem iter_succ (S : MaxPlusDepthSystem α) (n : Nat) (f : α) :
    S.iter (n + 1) f = S.comp (S.iter n f) f := rfl

/-! ### Elementary `Nat` arithmetic support -/

/-- Exponent monotonicity for a fixed base `b ≥ 1` (thin wrapper around
`Nat.pow_le_pow_right`). -/
theorem pow_le_pow_of_le {b m n : Nat} (hb : 1 ≤ b) (h : m ≤ n) :
    b ^ m ≤ b ^ n := Nat.pow_le_pow_right hb h

/-- For a base `b ≥ 1`, exponentiation commutes with `max`. -/
theorem pow_max_eq_max_pow (b m n : Nat) (hb : 1 ≤ b) :
    b ^ (max m n) = max (b ^ m) (b ^ n) := by
  rcases le_total m n with h | h
  · rw [max_eq_right h, max_eq_right (Nat.pow_le_pow_right hb h)]
  · rw [max_eq_left h, max_eq_left (Nat.pow_le_pow_right hb h)]

/-! ### The multiplicative bridge -/

/-- **Bridge theorem.**  The additive tropical bound on `depth` becomes a
multiplicative Lipschitz-style bound on `shadow`. -/
theorem shadow_comp_le (S : MaxPlusDepthSystem α) (b : Nat) (f g : α) (hb : 1 ≤ b) :
    S.shadow b (S.comp f g) ≤ b * max (S.shadow b f) (S.shadow b g) := by
  unfold shadow
  calc
    b ^ S.depth (S.comp f g)
        ≤ b ^ (max (S.depth f) (S.depth g) + 1) :=
          Nat.pow_le_pow_right hb (S.depth_comp_le f g)
    _ = b * b ^ (max (S.depth f) (S.depth g)) := by rw [pow_succ]; ring
    _ = b * max (b ^ S.depth f) (b ^ S.depth g) := by
          rw [pow_max_eq_max_pow _ _ _ hb]

/-! ### Stability under iteration -/

/-- The depth of the `n`-fold iterate grows at most linearly in `n`. -/
theorem depth_iter_succ_le (S : MaxPlusDepthSystem α) (n : Nat) (f : α) :
    S.depth (S.iter n f) ≤ S.depth f + n := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp [iter]
  | succ k ih =>
      rw [iter_succ]
      have hc := S.depth_comp_le (S.iter k f) f
      have hmax : max (S.depth (S.iter k f)) (S.depth f) ≤ S.depth f + k :=
        max_le ih (by omega)
      omega

/-- The multiplicative iterate bound: the shadow of the `n`-fold iterate grows at
most like `b ^ n`. -/
theorem shadow_iter_le (S : MaxPlusDepthSystem α) (b n : Nat) (f : α) (hb : 1 ≤ b) :
    S.shadow b (S.iter n f) ≤ b ^ n * S.shadow b f := by
  unfold shadow
  calc
    b ^ S.depth (S.iter n f)
        ≤ b ^ (S.depth f + n) := Nat.pow_le_pow_right hb (S.depth_iter_succ_le n f)
    _ = b ^ n * b ^ S.depth f := by rw [pow_add]; ring

import Mathlib

open Function Metric

noncomputable section

namespace TropicalRipsConnectivity

universe u
variable {α : Type u}

/-! ## §1. The Rips graph (self-contained re-statement) -/

/-- The **Rips graph** (Vietoris–Rips 1-skeleton) at scale `ε`: distinct points are
    adjacent iff within distance `ε`.  Re-stated from
    `Applications/PoincareData/MetricFiltration.lean` so this file builds standalone. -/
def ripsGraph (α : Type u) [PseudoMetricSpace α] (ε : ℝ) : SimpleGraph α where
  Adj x y := x ≠ y ∧ dist x y ≤ ε
  symm x y h := ⟨h.1.symm, by rw [dist_comm]; exact h.2⟩
  loopless := ⟨fun x h => h.1 rfl⟩

variable [PseudoMetricSpace α]

@[simp] lemma ripsGraph_adj_iff {ε : ℝ} {x y : α} :
    (ripsGraph α ε).Adj x y ↔ x ≠ y ∧ dist x y ≤ ε := Iff.rfl

/-- Filtration monotonicity: larger scale ⇒ larger graph. -/
theorem ripsGraph_mono {ε₁ ε₂ : ℝ} (h : ε₁ ≤ ε₂) :
    ripsGraph α ε₁ ≤ ripsGraph α ε₂ := by
  intro x y hxy
  exact ⟨hxy.1, hxy.2.trans h⟩

/-- Functoriality of connectivity: reachability is monotone in the scale. -/
theorem reachable_mono {ε₁ ε₂ : ℝ} (h : ε₁ ≤ ε₂) {x y : α}
    (hr : (ripsGraph α ε₁).Reachable x y) : (ripsGraph α ε₂).Reachable x y :=
  hr.mono (ripsGraph_mono h)

/-! ## §2. The general (Archimedean) bound -/

/-- **General bound.** In an arbitrary pseudometric space, a Rips walk of length `n` from
    `x` to `y` only certifies `dist x y ≤ n · ε`.  This is the "Archimedean leak":
    connectivity does *not* control the true distance.  Note: `0 ≤ ε` is *not* needed —
    if a positive-length edge exists then `ε ≥ dist ≥ 0` automatically. -/
theorem dist_le_of_walk_length {ε : ℝ} {x y : α}
    (p : (ripsGraph α ε).Walk x y) : dist x y ≤ p.length * ε := by
  induction' p with x y hxy p ih;
  · simp +decide;
  · simp +zetaDelta at *;
    linarith [ dist_triangle y hxy p, ih.2 ]

/-! ## §3. The ultrametric collapse -/

variable [IsUltrametricDist α]

/-- **Ultrametric collapse (lower bound).** Over an ultrametric space, *any* Rips walk
    from `x` to `y` at scale `ε` forces `dist x y ≤ ε`: the strong triangle inequality
    makes the bottleneck path distance equal the metric distance. -/
theorem reachable_dist_le {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 ≤ ε) {x y : α}
    (h : (ripsGraph α ε).Reachable x y) : dist x y ≤ ε := by
  -- By definition of reachability, there exists a walk from $x$ to $y$ in the Rips graph at scale $\epsilon$.
  obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ : ∃ p : (ripsGraph α ε).Walk x y, True := by
    exact ⟨ h.some, trivial ⟩;
  induction' p with x y hxy p ih;
  · simpa using hε;
  · rename_i h₁ h₂;
    exact le_trans ( IsUltrametricDist.dist_triangle_max y hxy p ) ( max_le ih.2 ( h₂ <| h₁.reachable ) )

/-- **Connectivity = sublevel test.** Over an ultrametric space, `x` and `y` are
    Rips-connected at scale `ε` iff `dist x y ≤ ε`. -/
theorem reachable_iff {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 ≤ ε) {x y : α} :
    (ripsGraph α ε).Reachable x y ↔ dist x y ≤ ε := by
  by_cases hxy : x = y <;> simp +decide [ *, ripsGraph ];
  exact ⟨ fun h => reachable_dist_le hε h, fun h => SimpleGraph.Adj.reachable ( by tauto ) ⟩

/-- The connectivity class of `x` is exactly the closed metric ball of radius `ε`. -/
theorem reachableSet_eq_closedBall {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 ≤ ε) (x : α) :
    {y | (ripsGraph α ε).Reachable x y} = Metric.closedBall x ε := by
  ext y
  simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, Metric.mem_closedBall, reachable_iff hε, dist_comm y x]

/-! ## §4. The tropical connectivity-threshold functor -/

/-- The **connectivity threshold**: the exact scale at which `x` and `y` merge in the
    Rips filtration.  Over an ultrametric space this equals the distance. -/
def connThreshold (x y : α) : ℝ := dist x y

/-- **Functorial tropical lower bound.** The connectivity-threshold functor lands in the
    tropical (max) semiring: it satisfies the strong/tropical triangle inequality. -/
theorem connThreshold_ultra (x y z : α) :
    connThreshold x z ≤ max (connThreshold x y) (connThreshold y z) :=
  dist_triangle_max x y z

/-- `dist x y` is the *least* scale connecting `x` and `y`: it is connected for every
    `ε ≥ dist x y`, and every connecting scale `ε` satisfies `ε ≥ dist x y`.  Hence the
    threshold is a certified, tight lower bound. -/
theorem rips_connectivity_lower_bound {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 ≤ ε) {x y : α} :
    (ripsGraph α ε).Reachable x y ↔ connThreshold x y ≤ ε := by
  simpa [connThreshold] using reachable_iff (α := α) hε (x := x) (y := y)

end TropicalRipsConnectivity

the functor `DepthFiltration.ofUltrametric` (concretely realized on `ℤ_[p]`).

## Conjecture 1 — Vanishing higher persistent homology (ultrametric Rips collapse)

**Statement.** For a finite ultrametric space `X`, the Vietoris–Rips complex at every scale
`ε ≥ 0` is homotopy equivalent to a disjoint union of points (its `π₀`); equivalently, all
reduced homology groups `H̃_n(Rips(X, ε))` vanish for `n ≥ 1`, at every scale.

**Why plausible.** `ripsReachable_iff` shows each Rips component is a *clique* (the whole
closed ε-ball), and the clique/Vietoris–Rips complex of a complete graph is a simplex, hence
contractible. The bridge file already proves the `π₀`/1-skeleton statement; this conjecture
is its higher-dimensional completion.

**Test / falsification.** Formalize "each component induces a complete graph" (immediate from
`ripsRel_trans`) and connect to a simplicial-complex contractibility lemma. A single
ultrametric point cloud with nontrivial `H_1` would falsify it.

## Conjecture 2 — Persistence diagrams of ultrametric spaces are dendrograms

**Statement.** The persistence module of `π₀` of the Rips filtration of a finite ultrametric
space is a **functor from `(ℝ, ≤)` to finite partitions** that is *monotone coarsening*, and
its barcode is in bijection with the merge events of single-linkage hierarchical clustering
(a rooted dendrogram). No `H_0` bar is ever "born after" another bar without a corresponding
ball-merge.

**Why plausible.** `ripsRel_mono` + `ripsSetoid` give a chain of coarsening equivalence
relations; the births/deaths of components are exactly the distinct values of the ultrametric.

**Test / falsification.** Define `numComponents X ε := Nat` (number of `ripsSetoid` classes)
and prove it is a monotone step function of `ε` whose jump set equals the image of `dist`.
Falsified by an ultrametric space whose component-count function has a jump at a non-distance
value.

## Conjecture 3 — Functoriality is full: every depth filtration is ultrametric

**Statement.** The functor `DepthFiltration.ofUltrametric` is *essentially surjective*: every
abstract `DepthFiltration X` (a nested family of equivalence relations) arises, up to
relabeling of depths, from a genuine ultrametric pseudometric on `X` via the schedule
`s n = 2^{-n}`. Concretely, `d(x,y) := 2^{-(sup {k | agree k x y})}` (with `d = 0` when the
set is unbounded) is an `IsUltrametricDist` pseudometric whose induced depth filtration
recovers the original `agree`.

**Why plausible.** The `agree_trans` axiom is exactly the ultrametric strong-triangle
inequality transported through `2^{-(·)}`; `agree_antitone` gives monotonicity of the sup.

**Test / falsification.** Construct `DepthFiltration.toUltrametric : DepthFiltration X →

ultrametric inequality after `2^{-(·)}` transport (it always can, so this should be provable).

**Statement.** For a finite set `S ⊆ ℤ_[p]`, the **connectivity threshold** of the Rips
filtration — the smallest `ε` at which `ripsGraph ℤ_[p] ε` restricted to `S` is connected —

largest "valuation gap" `max_{i} (v_i - v_{i-1})` along the sorted pairwise valuations.

**Why plausible.** `padic_dist_le_pow_iff` identifies Rips edges at scale `p^{-n}` with

**Statement.** Define the *Rips transitivity defect* of a metric space at scale `ε` as the

metric space it gives a tight, scale-independent upper bound on how much larger the Rips

path-length bound. Falsified by a metric space with zero defect that is not ultrametric, or by
a reachable pair exceeding the stated bound.

/-- In an ultrametric space the Rips relation is transitive: this is the strong
(non-Archimedean) triangle inequality `dist x z ≤ max (dist x y) (dist y z)`. -/
theorem ripsRel_trans {ε : ℝ} {x y z : α}
    (hxy : ripsRel ε x y) (hyz : ripsRel ε y z) : ripsRel ε x z :=
  le_trans (IsUltrametricDist.dist_triangle_max x y z) (max_le hxy hyz)

/-- Packaging the Rips relation as an `Equivalence` for a non-negative scale in an
ultrametric space. -/
theorem ripsRel_equivalence {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 ≤ ε) : Equivalence (ripsRel (α := α) ε) where
  refl x := ripsRel_refl hε x
  symm h := ripsRel_symm h
  trans hxy hyz := ripsRel_trans hxy hyz

/-- Rips-chain collapse: a chain of one-step Rips moves can be collapsed to a single
step in an ultrametric space (the case `0 ≤ ε` is needed for the empty/reflexive
chain). -/
theorem ripsRel_of_reflTransGen {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 ≤ ε) {x y : α}
    (h : Relation.ReflTransGen (ripsRel ε) x y) : ripsRel ε x y := by
  induction h with
  | refl => exact ripsRel_refl hε x
  | tail _ hbc ih => exact ripsRel_trans ih hbc

/-- Reachability via Rips chains coincides with single-step proximity. -/
theorem ripsReachable_iff {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 ≤ ε) {x y : α} :
    Relation.ReflTransGen (ripsRel ε) x y ↔ ripsRel ε x y :=
  ⟨ripsRel_of_reflTransGen hε, Relation.ReflTransGen.single⟩

/-- Rephrasing reachability directly in terms of distance. -/
theorem ripsReachable_iff_dist {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 ≤ ε) {x y : α} :
    Relation.ReflTransGen (ripsRel ε) x y ↔ dist x y ≤ ε :=
  ripsReachable_iff hε

/-- Rephrasing reachability as membership in a closed ball. -/
theorem ripsReachable_iff_mem_closedBall {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 ≤ ε) {x y : α} :
    Relation.ReflTransGen (ripsRel ε) x y ↔ y ∈ Metric.closedBall x ε := by
  rw [ripsReachable_iff_dist hε, Metric.mem_closedBall, dist_comm x y]

end Ultrametric

/-- A set `s` is a **Rips simplex** at scale `ε` when all pairs of distinct points in
`s` are within distance `ε`. -/
def IsRipsSimplex (ε : ℝ) (s : Set α) : Prop := s.Pairwise fun x y => dist x y ≤ ε

/-- Rips simplices are monotone in the scale. -/
theorem IsRipsSimplex.mono {ε ε' : ℝ} (hε : ε ≤ ε') {s : Set α}
    (h : IsRipsSimplex ε s) : IsRipsSimplex ε' s :=
  h.mono' fun _ _ hxy => le_trans hxy hε

/-- In an ultrametric space every closed ball is a Rips simplex at the same scale. -/
theorem isRipsSimplex_closedBall [IsUltrametricDist α] (x : α) (ε : ℝ) :
    IsRipsSimplex ε (Metric.closedBall x ε) := by
  intro a ha b hb _
  rw [Metric.mem_closedBall] at ha hb
  calc dist a b ≤ max (dist a x) (dist x b) := IsUltrametricDist.dist_triangle_max a x b
    _ ≤ ε := max_le ha ((dist_comm b x) ▸ hb)

end ValuationRipsBridge

# Future Directions — Valuation ↔ Vietoris–Rips bridge

Foundational results established in `Catalog/Bridges/ValuationRipsBridge.lean`:
in an ultrametric (non-Archimedean valuation) space the Vietoris–Rips proximity
relation is, for every scale `r ≥ 0`, an equivalence relation; Rips paths
collapse to Rips edges (`rips_chain_closed`); connected components are full
simplices (`class_isRipsSimplex`, `ball_isRipsSimplex`); the filtration is
monotone (`ripsRel_mono`, `IsRipsSimplex.mono`); and triangles are isosceles
(`ultrametric_isosceles`). The following conjectures extend this line.

## C1. Vanishing of higher Rips homology (ultrametric ⇒ degree-0 persistence)
For a finite ultrametric space `X` and any `r ≥ 0`, the geometric realization of
`Rips_r(X)` is homotopy equivalent to the discrete set of clusters
`X / ripsSetoid r`. Consequently every reduced simplicial homology group
`H̃_k(Rips_r(X))` vanishes for `k ≥ 1`, and persistent homology is concentrated
in degree 0. *Testable handle:* prove each connected component is a simplex (done
combinatorially) and that a simplex is contractible; then assemble per-component.

## C2. Dendrogram functoriality of the cluster map
The assignment `r ↦ (X / ripsSetoid r)` is a functor from `(ℝ≥0, ≤)` to `Set`
with surjective merge maps `π_{r,r'} : X/∼_r → X/∼_{r'}` for `r ≤ r'`, satisfying
`π_{r',r''} ∘ π_{r,r'} = π_{r,r''}`. Conjecture: this functor is a complete
invariant of the ultrametric — two finite ultrametric spaces are isometric iff
their cluster functors are naturally isomorphic. This formalizes the
ultrametric ↔ dendrogram correspondence of Carlsson–Mémoli.

## C3. Single-linkage recovers the valuation
Given an arbitrary finite metric space `(X, d)`, the single-linkage (maximal
sub-dominant) ultrametric `u(x,y) = min over paths of max edge` satisfies
`u ≤ d`, is ultrametric, and equals `d` exactly when `d` is already ultrametric.
Conjecture (and target): `rips_chain_closed` characterizes ultrametricity —
`d` is ultrametric iff `ReflTransGen (ripsRel r) = ripsRel r` for all `r ≥ 0`.

## C4. Stability / Lipschitz robustness of ultrametric clustering
For ultrametric `X`, the cluster partition is locally constant in `r` away from
the finite set of realized distances, and an additive perturbation of the metric
by `ε` (still ultrametric) changes cluster boundaries by at most `ε` in the
bottleneck sense. This is the ML-relevant robustness statement: hierarchical
clustering on valuation data is stable, with an explicit modulus.

## C5. Nerve/Čech agreement and exact reconstruction
For ultrametric `X`, the Vietoris–Rips complex and the Čech complex of closed
`r`-balls coincide (both are the disjoint union of cluster simplices), so the
Nerve Lemma holds on the nose without a "good cover" hypothesis. Conjecture:
this self-agreement characterizes ultrametricity among metric spaces and yields
exact reconstruction of `X` from its Rips filtration up to isometry (cf. C2).
